description: Frontier-paydown chain for the Schur-Weyl Markov weight w_(1, 1, 1)(q) at λ = (1, 1, 1).  Together with `schur-weyl-weight-3.derivation.json` (covering λ=(3)) this completes the per-λ coverage of n=3 partitions, discharging the last SCRIPT_CITED weight step in the proton Markov-trace assembly chain.  Trust profile is {axiom: 1, mathlib-cited: 2, derived: 1, script-cited: 0, computational: 0} — fully-trusted modulo the AXIOM (Hecke energy + Schur + Wedderburn).

steps.name: q-integer [k]_q := (q^k − q^{-k})/(q − q^{-1})
steps.operation: Define [k]_q := (q^k − q^{-k}) / (q − q^{-1}); the denominator (q − q^{-1}) is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale.  Same definition as in `schur-weyl-weight-3` and `sigma-shell-A2-closed-form`.

steps.name: Hook-length set for λ = (1, 1, 1)
steps.operation: For λ = (1, 1, 1) ⊢ 3, the hook lengths are [3, 2, 1].  The number of parts is l(λ) = 3 (so the weight exponent is n − l(λ) = 0).
steps.notes: Mathlib's `Mathlib.Combinatorics.Young.YoungDiagram` exposes `hookLength`; the values are read off the Young diagram combinatorially.

steps.name: Wedderburn block dimension f_(1, 1, 1)
steps.operation: From Wedderburn, H_3(q) = ⊕_λ M_{f_λ}(K(q)) where f_λ counts standard Young tableaux of shape λ.  For λ = (1, 1, 1), f_λ = 1.

steps.name: Markov weight w_(1, 1, 1)(q)
steps.operation: Apply the Markov weight convention w_λ(q) := (q − q^{-1})^(n − l(λ)) · ∏_{x ∈ λ} [h_x]_q^{-1}.  For (1, 1, 1) this evaluates to 1 / ([3]_q · [2]_q · [1]_q).  Same convention as in `schur-weyl-weight-3.derivation.json`.
steps.notes: Pure algebra: substitute the hook lengths from step 2 and the exponent (n − l(λ)) from step 2 (hook-length data) into the convention.  The (q − q^{-1})^(n − l(λ)) prefactor arises from Hoefsmit's normalisation of the simple reps of H_n(q); it ensures the Markov stabilisation tr_M(α σ_n) = z · tr_M(α) holds with the canonical stabilisation parameter z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}).
